semantics.note: The proposition keeps both parts: no profit on the data centers and little generative AI revenue. It softens 'anything resembling a profit' slightly but is faithful.

contract.note: Reading 'these data centers' as AI capacity and judging revenue against capex fits the passage. But the result depends on choices the speaker never made: AI-only versus cloud-wide profit, and absolute versus relative revenue.

evidence.note: Microsoft disclosed an AI run rate above $13B. That is a run rate and a company disclosure. The packet has no capex figure to compare it with, so it cannot settle 'not much'.
AWS made $10.2B operating income in Q2 2025, but for the whole cloud segment. The AI share is not broken out, so this neither shows nor rules out profit on AI data centers.
AI depreciation costs weigh on a cloud segment that stays profitable. AI-specific profit is not disclosed either way.

reviews.rationale: No company reports AI-specific profit, so the packet cannot show either profit or no profit on AI data centers. Cloud profits only count against the claim under a broader reading. The packet covers only Microsoft revenue and AWS: there are no capex figures and no data on Google or Meta, so the 'not much revenue' comparison cannot be made.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: 'Appears' marks an inference from evidence, not a probability, and the stated quantity is firm. The window and the $10B threshold are kept.

contract.note: Reading 'burned' as net cash burn is the ordinary meaning, and the 'plausibly appeared so' wording allows for the hedge. Under any reasonable reading, the bounding figures rule out $10B in two months.

evidence.note: First-half 2025 burn of $2.5B caps June at about $2.5B. Reaching $10B would then need $7.5B or more in roughly five weeks.
The full-year 2025 burn target of $8.5B, reported after the window, is below $10B. It is a target, not an actual.
The first-half net loss of $13.5B is mostly a non-cash remeasurement. Net loss is not cash burn.

The listed available_at (2026-03-01) conflicts with the article's own June 2026 date. Both are before the evaluation date. The full-year operating loss of about $20.9B averages about $3.5B per two months, which is also short of $10B.

reviews.rationale: Reported figures put first-half 2025 cash burn at $2.5B and the full-year target at $8.5B. Even the broader operating-loss figure averages about $3.5B per two months. A burn of $10B or more from June to early August is not plausible. The figure appears to treat fundraising as burn.

semantics.note: 'Doesn't seem' is kept. It describes how Perplexity's finances looked on the public record, not a probabilistic forecast.

contract.note: Reading 'close to profitable' as near break-even, judged on reporting before the post, is an ordinary reading that matches the hedge. The choice of period was the evaluator's.

evidence.note: Reported 2024 figures: about $65M cash burn on about $34M revenue. Burn near twice revenue is far from break-even, and this was reported before the post.
An $80M run rate in January 2025 shows growth, but the report gives nothing suggesting break-even.

reviews.rationale: The latest reporting before the post shows cash burn nearly double revenue. Nothing in the packet suggests Perplexity was near break-even. The 'three years and a billion dollars' premise was not checked, but the core claim holds on the public record.
